title: GAP Waiver Premier 150 Starting Balance: Days Added by a Due-Date Change
content:
For a GAP Waiver Addenda claim on a GAP Waiver Premier 150 addendum, the Premier starting balance capitalizes the days by which a due-date change on the Retail Installment Contracts contract moved the next due date later.

The change read is the latest due-date change the contract records: the one with the latest effective date. Where two due-date changes share that date, the one recorded first counts. The days moved are the calendar days from the change's old next due date to its new next due date.

**Rule.**

- When the change took effect on or before the date of loss and moved the next due date later by more than 15 days, 15 days are capitalized.
- When it took effect on or before the date of loss and moved the next due date later by 1 to 15 days, those days are capitalized.
- Otherwise none are capitalized. This covers a change that took effect after the date of loss, a change that did not move the date later, and a contract with no due-date change.

The added days capitalized add to the opening principal. The amount added is the amount financed times the original annual percentage rate divided by 100, times those days, divided by 365, rounded half-up to the cent.

| Latest due-date change | Days capitalized |
|---|---|
| effective before the loss, moved 22 days later | 15 |
| effective before the loss, moved 15 days later | 15 |
| effective before the loss, moved 9 days later | 9 |
| effective on the date of loss, moved 9 days later | 9 |
| effective after the loss | none |

*Hypothetical case.* On 14000.00 financed at 21 percent, 9 capitalized days add 72.49 to the opening principal.
